candidates.exact_span: The limit for viable helminth ova is less than one per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a numeric helminth-ova limit and whether sampling/comparison is tied to pre-treatment versus post-treatment timing; different readings of 'either before or following pathogen treatment' could change which measurements are compared and when monitoring is required.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 4 - The density of enteric viruses in the sewage sludge shall be less than one Plaque- forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed or at the time the sludge is prepared for sale or give away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets an enforceable numeric enteric-virus limit and multiple alternative compliance-time triggers; interpretation of which trigger applies (use/disposal versus bagged sale/give-away preparation) could change the applicable limit period, required monitoring episode, and whether absent numeric results reflect conditional non-requirement versus missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The density of viable helminth ova in the sewage sludge shall be less than one per four grams of total solids (dry weigh t basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or dispose d or at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or give away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Repeats a numeric helminth-ova limit under Alternative 4 with use/disposal or bagged-preparation timing; different readings of the operative time and event could change limit applicability, monitoring obligations, and classification of no-result periods.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 5 - Sewage sludge shall be treated by one of the Processes to Further Reduce Pathogens (PFRP) described in 503 Appendix B. PFRPs include composting, heat drying, heat treatment, and thermophilic aerobic digestion.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides a process-based compliance pathway without an ordinary numeric density limit in this span; whether this alternative is selected affects whether numeric limit comparison applies and how missing numeric monitoring results should be interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 6 - Sewage sludge shall be treated by a process that is equivalent to a Process to Further Reduce Pathogens, if individually approved by the Pathogen Equivalency Committee representing the EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes an equivalency-based process pathway whose authorization depends on individual EPA approval; interpretation of whether that approval exists could change whether numeric limits apply and whether absent measurements reflect non-required conditional monitoring versus unresolved missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Alternatives 2 and 3 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class B sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Restricts which Class B compliance alternatives are permit-valid in Texas; different readings of authorization could exclude process-based pathways and force reliance on numeric or other authorized alternatives, changing applicable limits, monitoring requirements, and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 1 - Seven random samples of the sewage sludge shall be collected for one monitoring episode at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the number of samples, randomness, single monitoring episode, and event timing for Class B compliance; interpretation of these terms could change whether monitoring was required for a given period and whether missing sample evidence is a documented no-requirement state or inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The geometric mean of the density of fecal coliform in the samples collected shall be less than either 2,000,000 MPN per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) or 2,000,000 Colony Forming Units per gram of total solids (dry weight basis).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the enforceable Class B fecal-coliform numeric limit and allows two reporting units (MPN versus CFU); interpretation of which unit applies to reported measurements and how the geometric mean is computed across seven samples could change exceedance determinations and monitoring-evaluation outcomes.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 2 - Sewage sludge shall be treated in one of the Processes to significantly Reduce Pathogens described in 503 Appendix B.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Offers a process-based Class B compliance route that is not numeric in this span and is separately restricted for Texas permits; whether this alternative is available affects numeric limit applicability and how absent density results are categorized.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 3 - Sewage sludge shall be treated in a process that is equivalent to a PSRP, if individually approved by the Pathogen Equivalency Committee representing the EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides an equivalency-based Class B process pathway contingent on individual approval and subject to the Texas authorization restriction; interpretation of permit authorization and approval status could change monitoring obligations and missing-evidence semantics for non-numeric compliance.
